answer: One defense: latency-fingerprint clustering at the harbor gateway. Each epoch, agents answer unpredictable beacon probes; the gateway seals replies with a fresh session cipher while logging round-trip jitter and clock skew. Across epochs these traces form a timing plume that cannot be faked in parallel: one operator running M puppets on one machine shows overlapping jitter, so the cluster collapses them into a single voting weight. Attackers must then buy M distinct network routes, VPN exits and hardware clocks - linear cost in M, not one cheap script - while honest nodes pay nothing extra.
